agent_vs_you: The agent's three prompts are good on everything they mention: qwen with lettering, the exact name with the ampersand, one standalone mark each, and three genuinely different ideas (wheel, winding route, MM monogram) with different layouts. None of them says green, black or white, so qwen drew a clean black-on-white logo three times. The planner never saw the palette: the sheet filled direction with the enum value "stated" and kept "Simple green and black on white" only in that field's quote, and plan.js builds the SHEET lines as `field: value (source)`, so the planner read `direction: stated (stated)`. Its desired_state confirms it ("...each featuring the exact name and a small, genuinely different symbol"), and the planner's own rule "THE USER'S WORDS ARE THE SPEC ... 'green and black on white' is green, black and pure white" could not fire on words it was never shown. I would lead every prompt with the palette and say which part is which colour (the symbol green, the name black, the ground pure white), because qwen defaults to monochrome for a "clean logo".

fix: Carry the user's look into the planner. In plan.js print each stated field's quote next to its value (e.g. `direction: stated — "Simple green and black on white"`), or in sheet.js fill `style` whenever direction=stated, not only when direction=needed. Extend guard() in plan.js so every colour word in the stated direction quote must appear in every image/image-edit prompt (prepend "In green and black on pure white:" when it is missing). The same lost-quote path dropped "watercolor" in D22b and "soft watercolours" in J50a.
